Subject: Novellus: Dedicated capacity and SLO headroom modeling

Hi Sara / Devon —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our conversation I sketched a proposal to map the target SLOs you described to a dedicated GPU slab strategy and an initial tokens/sec budget. High level: we can hit the 95th percentile latency targets for your multi-turn summarization and retrieval-assisted agents with a mix of quantized Llama-3-20B variants and a small fleet of A100-equivalent nodes, but there are important tradeoffs around concurrency and cold-starts.

Key ask from you: confirm the steady-state requests per minute (RPM) and % of requests that hit the retrieval path vs. direct generation. I used the numbers you mentioned on the call (avg 120 RPM, retrieval in ~30% of requests) for the first pass.

Quick summary (first-pass numbers attached):
- Workload profile: multi-turn chat, avg prompt + context = 1,200 tokens, avg generation = 450 tokens.
- Target SLOs: p95 latency <= 1.2s for direct generation, <= 1.8s when retrieval pipeline is active.
- Modeled model variants: Llama-3-20B (8-bit quant) for baseline; fallback to Llama-3-7B (int8) for burst spikes.
- Estimated steady tokens/sec: ~900 tokens/sec sustained across fleet for target p95.
- Safety headroom: 35% (to cover bursts, KV-cache cold misses, and scheduled maintenance).
- Recommended reserved capacity: 6 dedicated GPUs (A100-equivalent) with autoscale burst to +2 nodes.

Attachments: novellus-projection-v1.xlsx — includes tokens/sec model, latency curves, and cost sensitivity.

Next steps: once you confirm RPM and retrieval ratio I’ll loop in Priyom + Hannah to convert this into a per-slab allocation and confirm the p95 simulation. Kimberly, can you flag any procurement timing or contract constraints?

Thanks,
Marcus

Thanks Marcus — this is a helpful start. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- RPM: the product team expects an initial steady-state of ~150 RPM with peaks up to 600 RPM during business hours over the first 90 days.
- Retrieval ratio: closer to 45% of requests will hit retrieval + re-rank.
- Cold start concerns: we currently expect many cold prefixes for new customer sessions; that may increase KV-cache misses early on.

Can you run the numbers with 150 RPM steady, 45% retrieval ratio, and a 20% cold-cache penalty? Also — we'll want an explicit fallback plan that keeps responses under 3s even during sustained 3x bursts.

Devon from procurement is CC'd — procurement will want an estimate for committed capacity, expected monthly token volumes, and a timeline for Dedicated activation.

Marcus / team / Sara —

Attached are the updated projections and a concise runbook. Summary highlights below (full numbers in novellus-projection-v1.xlsx and p95 curves in slo-mapping.pdf):

Summary (engineered model):
- Input assumptions used: 150 RPM steady (2.5 RPS), bursts to 600 RPM (10 RPS) sustained up to 30 minutes; retrieval in 45% of requests; cold-cache penalty modeled as +20% token generation time and 1 additional KV fetch step.
- Baseline fleet (measured per-node): Quantized Llama-3-20B (int8) delivers ~1250 tokens/sec peak per A100-equivalent node at 1.2s p95 under direct-gen conditions; with retrieval path active (fetch + re-rank) effective tokens/sec per node drops to ~760 tokens/sec at 1.8s p95.
- Recommended committed slab: 5 reserved GPUs sized to match steady-state with 35% operational headroom. Rationale: 5 nodes cover steady 2.5 RPS without hitting p95 > target; headroom covers short spikes and maintenance.
- Burst policy: autoscale +2 nodes (to 7 total) for sustained peaks; additionally enable model fallback (20B -> 7B) to manage sustained 3x bursts while preserving <3s response at p95.
- Safety buffer scenarios: with +50% conservative buffer we recommend 8 reserved GPUs (autoscale +3) — useful if Novellus wants SLA-backed commitments for holiday peaks.

Costs & tokens:
- Modeled monthly tokens (90-day ramp): ~1.1B tokens/month steady (generation + retrieval tokens), peak month up to ~2.8B tokens.
- Token-level cost sensitivity included in spreadsheet (sheet: cost_sensitivity).

Operational notes and mitigations:
- KV-cache warmup: add a short TTL-based prefetch for high-value prefixes and a warmup job that primes cache for top 10% of customers during onboarding windows. This reduces cold-cache penalty by ~60% in simulations.
- Latency tracing: enable per-request tracing (sampling 5%) to validate p95 in production and tune batching windows.
- Fallback policy: prefer 7B fallback for low-latency paths; automatically shift traffic back when node-level token/sec < 60% of expected.

Attachments: novellus-projection-v1.xlsx (updated), slo-mapping.pdf (p95 charts), novellus-qna-screenshots.png (example user flows instrumented).

If this looks good Sara / Devon, we can convert the recommended committed slab (5 GPUs, autoscale +2) into a procurement sheet with monthly token estimates and a recommended contract cadence (quarterly ramp).

Thanks — Priyom
